app_purpose: Regular expression for matching semver versions inside arbitrary text; a tiny, extremely widely-depended-on utility (used by release tooling, changelog/version parsers, CI scripts). The sink is the single exported regex `semverRegex()` applied to untrusted input via `.test()`/`.match()`.
root_cause: ReDoS / catastrophic (exponential) regex backtracking in the pre-release / build-metadata group of the exported semver regex (index.js) (CWE-1333)

v0.ref: npm 3.1.1 (pre CVE-2021-3795). index.js: `/(?<=^v?|\sv?)(?:0|[1-9]\d*)\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*)\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*)(?:-(?:0|[1-9]\d*|[\da-z-]*[a-z-][\da-z-]*)(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*|[\da-z-]*[a-z-][\da-z-]*))*)?(?:\+[\da-z-]+(?:\.[\da-z-]+)*)?(?=$|\s)/ig`. Unbounded greedy pre-release identifier `[\da-z-]*[a-z-][\da-z-]*` inside an unbounded dotted repetition `(?:\.(...))*`, terminated by the lookahead `(?=$|\s)`; a dotted run of ambiguous identifiers followed by a lookahead-failing char backtracks catastrophically -> CVE-2021-3795.

v1.ref: npm 3.1.3 (CVE-2021-3795 fix = TARGET; 3.1.2 was an earlier still-exploitable attempt). index.js: `/(?:(?<=^v?|\sv?)(?:(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,9})\.){2}(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,9})(?:-(?:0|[1-9]\d*?|[\da-z-]*?[a-z-][\da-z-]*?){0,100}(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*?|[\da-z-]*?[a-z-][\da-z-]*?))*?){0,100}(?:\+[\da-z-]+?(?:\.[\da-z-]+?)*?){0,100}\b){1,200}/gi`. The rewrite bounds the numeric fields (`\d{0,9}`), makes identifiers lazy (`*?`), swaps the trailing `(?=$|\s)` for `\b`, and CAPS the repetitions with `{0,100}` / `{1,200}`. This closes the CVE-2021-3795 vector, BUT it INTRODUCES two nested `{0,100}` bounded groups in the pre-release; a `-.--`-style payload whose trailing space fails the `\b` drives exponential backtracking across the nested bounds -> CVE-2021-43307 residual. INCOMPLETE FIX.
v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:28133 (Express service, POST /check; docker compose --profile v1 up -d)

build.strategy: node:18-slim, `npm i express@4 semver-regex@<ver>` per profile via build-arg SEMVER_REGEX_VERSION (3.1.1/3.1.3/3.1.4). A REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js) validates a user-supplied version string with the REAL published package: `const ok = semverRegex().test(req.body.version)` on `POST /check` — the documented sink — with no vendored/edited source. The regex runs SYNCHRONOUSLY on the Node event loop, so a catastrophic input HANGS the HTTP response (server-side ReDoS). The oracle triggers it via an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measures the round-trip latency.
build.host_safety: the ReDoS is observed as external HTTP latency with a 10s client read timeout (a hang is recorded as ~10000ms, never an unbounded host wait). Each container is cpus=1.0, mem_limit=512m, stop_grace_period=2s. Because a synchronous regex permanently wedges Node's single-threaded event loop (a running regex cannot be interrupted), the oracle measures every payload against a FRESH server (kill + `up -d` between probes) so a slow probe never poisons the next. Payload lengths are tiny and bounded (original 95 chars, residual 63 chars, benign 13 chars) — the blow-up is pure-CPU exponential backtracking on a short input, flat memory. A fresh regex is built per request via `semverRegex()` so the `g`-flag lastIndex is always 0.
build.harness_note: semver-regex v3 ships a plain single-file index.js (`module.exports = () => /.../gi`, CommonJS) required directly by the Express service (`require('semver-regex')`). `semverRegex()` returns the identical real regex on all three versions. The service exposes GET /health and POST /check {version} -> {ok, server_ms}; the differential is the response latency of POST /check, triggered from OUTSIDE the container.

mechanism.summary: semver-regex exports ONE regex applied to untrusted input. (V0, 3.1.1) the pre-release group `(?:-(?:0|[1-9]\d*|[\da-z-]*[a-z-][\da-z-]*)(?:\.(?:...))*)?` uses an unbounded greedy ambiguous identifier inside an unbounded dotted repetition, closed by the lookahead `(?=$|\s)`; a dotted run of ambiguous identifiers (`a-a.`x N) followed by a lookahead-failing `!` forces catastrophic backtracking -> CVE-2021-3795. (V1, 3.1.3) the fix rewrites the regex: numeric fields bounded to `\d{0,9}`, identifiers made lazy, `(?=$|\s)` -> `\b`, and repetitions CAPPED with `{0,100}`/`{1,200}`. This closes the CVE-2021-3795 vector, BUT the rewrite nests TWO `{0,100}` bounded quantifiers in the pre-release: `(?:-(?:...){0,100}(?:\.(?:...))*?){0,100}`. A payload `0.0.1-` + `-.--`x N + ` ` (trailing space fails the new `\b`) explores a ~100x100 backtracking state space per anchor -> exponential blow-up -> CVE-2021-43307 (INCOMPLETE FIX). (V2, 3.1.4) the follow-up makes every bounded repetition LAZY (`{0,100}?`, `{1,200}?`, `{0,9}?`), collapsing the nested state space -> residual closed. Note the V0 (unbounded) and V1 (nested-bounded) forms are structurally different, so each CVE's vector is fast on the OTHER's regex — a clean same-sink, sequential-patch incomplete fix.
mechanism.original_sink: index.js exported regex — unbounded greedy pre-release identifier + dotted repetition + `(?=$|\s)` lookahead
mechanism.residual_sink: index.js exported regex — the newly introduced nested `{0,100}` bounded pre-release groups + `\b` anchor
mechanism.original_payload: '1.2.3-' + 'a-a.'.repeat(22) + '!'  (len 95) — dotted run of ambiguous pre-release identifiers, trailing '!' fails the V0 `(?=$|\s)` lookahead
mechanism.residual_payload: '0.0.1-' + '-.--'.repeat(14) + ' '  (len 63) — dash/dot run in the pre-release, trailing space fails the V1 `\b` anchor and blows up the nested {0,100} groups
mechanism.benign_payload: '1.2.3-alpha.1'  (len 13) — a normal semver with a well-formed pre-release; matches cleanly on all versions

evidence.fix_reference: npm 3.1.3 (CVE-2021-3795 fix = TARGET; 3.1.2 was an earlier still-exploitable attempt). index.js: `/(?:(?<=^v?|\sv?)(?:(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,9})\.){2}(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,9})(?:-(?:0|[1-9]\d*?|[\da-z-]*?[a-z-][\da-z-]*?){0,100}(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*?|[\da-z-]*?[a-z-][\da-z-]*?))*?){0,100}(?:\+[\da-z-]+?(?:\.[\da-z-]+?)*?){0,100}\b){1,200}/gi`. The rewrite bounds the numeric fields (`\d{0,9}`), makes identifiers lazy (`*?`), swaps the trailing `(?=$|\s)` for `\b`, and CAPS the repetitions with `{0,100}` / `{1,200}`. This closes the CVE-2021-3795 vector, BUT it INTRODUCES two nested `{0,100}` bounded groups in the pre-release; a `-.--`-style payload whose trailing space fails the `\b` drives exponential backtracking across the nested bounds -> CVE-2021-43307 residual. INCOMPLETE FIX.; npm 3.1.4 (CVE-2021-43307 fix). index.js: `/(?:(?<=^v?|\sv?)(?:(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,9}?)\.){2}(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,9}?)(?:-(?:0|[1-9]\d*?|[\da-z-]*?[a-z-][\da-z-]*?){0,100}?(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*?|[\da-z-]*?[a-z-][\da-z-]*?))*?){0,100}?(?:\+[\da-z-]+?(?:\.[\da-z-]+?)*?){0,100}?\b){1,200}?/gi`. Every bounded repetition made LAZY (`{0,9}?`, `{0,100}?`, `{1,200}?`); the nested pre-release groups no longer expand into an exponential state space -> residual closed (linear).
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Both CVEs are exponential ReDoS in the SAME index.js exported regex. The CVE-2021-3795 rewrite (through 3.1.3) capped the pre-release repetitions with nested {0,100} bounds; JFrog (XRAY-211349, GHSA-4x5v-gmq8-25ch) showed that nesting itself is still exponentially backtrackable via `'0.0.1-' + '-.--'.repeat(i) + ' '`, which required the 3.1.4 fix (making the bounds lazy). Textbook same-sink incomplete fix.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 to a REAL Express HTTP service (per HARD POLICY: no in-process library trigger). Built from the REAL published npm packages express@4 + semver-regex@3.1.1/3.1.3/3.1.4 on node:18-slim (no source edits). app/server.js exposes POST /check {version} -> `semverRegex().test(version)` running SYNCHRONOUSLY on the event loop; the ReDoS is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measured as server-side response latency. Regex evolution verified verbatim from each version's index.js (3.1.1 unbounded-greedy + (?=$|\s); 3.1.3 CVE-2021-3795 fix = nested {0,100} bounds + \b; 3.1.4 CVE-2021-43307 fix = bounds made lazy). Confirmed on real Docker (cpus=1.0, mem 512m, stop_grace 2s; fresh server per probe so a wedged event loop never poisons the next): original vector '1.2.3-'+'a-a.'x22+'!' hangs on V0 (HTTP 10s timeout) and is ~6-7ms on V1 & V2; residual vector '0.0.1-'+'-.--'x14+' ' is ~6.5ms on V0, hangs on V1 (HTTP 10s timeout, INCOMPLETE FIX), ~6.4ms on V2; benign '1.2.3-alpha.1' <=7ms everywhere. residual V1/V2 latency separation ~1563x (well over 50x). Same exported regex, sequential ReDoS patches, distinct CVEs / distinct fixed versions (3.1.3 vs 3.1.4).
